record.title: Language models use experimental records to predict research outcomes in fixed evaluations
record.summary: In an October 8 preprint, Wang and colleagues report that language models prompted with records of prior experiments rank unseen research interventions more accurately in five fixed research environments and improve experiment selection in their evaluations. They also report gains in five multi-round OLMo3-100M simulations. The results are author-reported: some cross-environment uncertainty intervals include zero, transfer evidence is limited to autoregressive pretraining, and independent reproduction and deployed research value remain unestablished.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across five author-reported research environments, conditioning language-model outcome predictions on prior experiments increased mean Spearman correlation for unseen interventions from 0.506 to 0.774. The experiments use fixed environment panels and splits.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For cross-environment prediction across five autoregressive pretraining targets, records from other environments increased macro Spearman correlation from 0.628 to 0.729 and reduced macro-average Regret@3 by 52.2% relative to a no-record predictor. Appendix D reports paired-bootstrap intervals that include zero for some target comparisons.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In five eight-round OLMo3-100M Autoresearch evaluations with 24 intervention selections per run, the authors report that in-environment and cross-environment records increased mean final best gain by 15.8% and 11.6%, respectively, versus the no-record setting.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The reported results do not establish independent reproducibility, transfer across arbitrary research domains, or improved real-world research productivity beyond these fixed and author-run evaluation settings.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported experiments and extracted metrics were not independently reproduced or recomputed from raw records in this review.
Cross-environment results cover five autoregressive pretraining targets; some paired-bootstrap target intervals include zero, while transfer to other research domains is not established.
The multi-round outcome evidence consists of five author-run OLMo3-100M evaluations with a fixed selection budget; deployment value and total data, inference and execution costs are not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported effects transfer to working research agents, accumulated experimental records could reduce wasted compute and improve which costly interventions researchers execute, shifting the value of durable experiment data. Current evidence is limited to fixed author-run panels, with cross-environment uncertainty and domain-transfer gaps, so the consequence is meaningful but not yet operationally established.
limitations: Evidence is one author-submitted arXiv paper; reported evaluations have not been independently reproduced here.

The prediction tables use fixed environment panels and splits; the paper reports 2,653 records across nine environments and 171,862 H100 GPU-hours of prior experiments, but these totals do not establish generality.
Cross-environment evaluation is limited to five autoregressive pretraining targets, and Appendix D pointwise paired-bootstrap intervals include zero for some target comparisons.
Multi-round evidence comes from five eight-round OLMo3-100M evaluations with 24 selections each; it does not establish gains in deployed research programs.
The authors state that data acquisition, inference and experiment execution costs all matter; the paper's results do not demonstrate a net productivity or cost advantage across settings.
brief.summary: In an October 8 preprint, Wang and colleagues report that language models prompted with records of prior experiments rank unseen research interventions more accurately in five fixed research environments and improve experiment selection in their evaluations. They also report gains in five multi-round OLMo3-100M simulations. The results are author-reported: some cross-environment uncertainty intervals include zero, transfer evidence is limited to autoregressive pretraining, and independent reproduction and deployed research value remain unestablished.

technical.claimed_result: The authors report a mean within-environment Spearman increase from 0.506 to 0.774 across five panels; cross-environment macro Spearman increased from 0.628 to 0.729 across five autoregressive pretraining targets; and records improved the reported final best gain in five multi-round OLMo3-100M runs by 15.8% (within-environment) and 11.6% (cross-environment).
technical.demonstrated_result: The inspected primary preprint documents the authors' design and reported results, including fixed-panel evaluations and paired-bootstrap uncertainty intervals. the research desk did not independently reproduce the experiments; performance effects remain CLAIMED.
technical.mechanism: A language model receives descriptions of an environment, candidate interventions and records of prior experiments, then predicts intervention outcomes. The predicted ranking guides a fixed-budget selection; executed outcomes can be added to the record history for subsequent rounds.
technical.regime: Author-run evaluations use 2,653 records from nine research environments. Within-environment predictions use fixed held-out panels; cross-environment transfer uses records from other environments for five autoregressive pretraining targets; multi-round results use five eight-round OLMo3-100M simulations and 24 selections per run.
technical.strongest_baseline: No-record language-model prediction (W0) is the principal comparison; matched kNN and ridge predictors receive the same records in prediction and selection evaluations. Cross-environment intervals are target-specific and include zero for some comparisons.

brief.title: Language models use experimental records to predict research outcomes in fixed evaluations
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported gains generalize, persistent experimental records could help research agents avoid lower-value runs and spend scarce compute on stronger candidates. The paper reports sizeable improvements in its fixed evaluations, but no independent reproduction, broad domain transfer or deployed-program cost advantage has been established.
